narrative:
The model estimated a 93.3% probability that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt. Because admission was tied to predicted bar success, that high failure risk led to your application being denied.

The strongest signal was your third-year class standing. You were in decile 1, while accepted students averaged around decile 5.79, and this pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Your first-year class standing was the second most influential factor; you were also in decile 1 there, compared with an accepted-student average of about 6.00, which also pushed toward failure. Your LSAT score was the third most important factor: a score of 31 is below the accepted-student average of 37.18, adding further risk to the prediction.

To improve your chances if you reapply, focus on demonstrating stronger academic preparation, especially in advanced law-school coursework, and consider intensive LSAT preparation and a retake if feasible. Meet with an admissions advisor to discuss what evidence would most convincingly address the model’s concern, and ask whether additional coursework, work experience, or a clear explanation of any past academic difficulty could strengthen a future application.
